title: Minor's Statement of Consent (Texas)
about: A minor's written statement of why Texas law lets them consent to their own care, which a clinician may rely on (Family Code 32.003(f), 32.004(b)(3)).

licence.terms: CC0 1.0: dedicated to the public domain. Use and adapt it freely, with no credit needed.

blocks.text: In Texas, a minor can agree to some care without a parent or guardian. Check each reason that is true for you. We can rely on what you write here.

blocks.label: Why I can agree to my own care
items: I am on active duty in the armed services of the United States.
I am 16 or older. I live apart from my parents or guardian, and I manage my own money.
I want to be checked or treated for a disease that must be reported to the health department, such as some sexually transmitted infections.
I am unmarried and pregnant, and I want care for the pregnancy, other than abortion.
I want to be checked or treated for drug or chemical addiction or dependency, or a problem from drug or chemical use.
I want counseling for suicide prevention, for chemical addiction or dependency, or for sexual, physical or emotional abuse.

blocks.label: Anything else about why I can agree

blocks.text: Texas law lets your clinician tell your parent or guardian about the care you get or need, with or without your consent. Ask us how we decide.
